contracts.commit_point: src/dungeon_agents/main.py:378 — `result = runner.run_sync(game_master, conversation, hooks=tool_hooks)`; the SDK raises InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered at this call before the model processes the input (caught at src/dungeon_agents/main.py:379), the refusal return completes at src/dungeon_agents/main.py:391, and the blocked message is dropped from history at src/dungeon_agents/main.py:742.
contracts.declared_mechanism: OpenAI Agents SDK input guardrail: `build_injection_guardrail(settings)` returns an `@input_guardrail`-decorated `injection_guardrail` attached to the Agent via `input_guardrails=[...]` (src/dungeon_agents/agents/game_master.py:156). Layer 1: deterministic `detect_injection` regex patterns over the reduced input text, returning GuardrailFunctionOutput(tripwire_triggered=True) with output_info blocked_by=pattern:<label> on match. Layer 2: for inputs surviving layer 1, an LLM judge is run via Runner.run(judge, text) and the tripwire fires if the verdict indicates injection. On trip, the SDK raises InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered, which `_play_turn` catches, prints an in-character refusal panel, and returns (None, conversation, None); the main loop then pops the blocked message (conversation.pop()) so it never poisons the history.
contracts.forbidden_condition: A prompt-injection/manipulation message being processed by the Game Master agent — i.e., reaching the model run at runner.run_sync — or a blocked injection message persisting in the conversation history after a refused turn.
pending_binding_information: Exact content of the JUDGE_INJECTION verdict token and the judge's configuration: src/dungeon_agents/agents/injection_judge.py is not among the supplied views.

SDK-side guarantee that input guardrails evaluate before the first model call is asserted only by repository comments/docstrings (src/dungeon_agents/agents/game_master.py:146-149; src/dungeon_agents/agents/guardrails.py:4-7); the agents SDK runtime source is not supplied.
Behavior of the guardrail when the layer-2 LLM judge call fails (exception inside Runner.run(judge, text)) — block-open vs. fail-open — is not specified in the supplied source.
Efficacy of the string reduction for non-string structured user_input (`str(user_input)` at src/dungeon_agents/agents/guardrails.py:47) is not established for structured input lists.
contracts.protected_operation: The Game Master turn driven by a real player action: the player message appended to `conversation` (src/dungeon_agents/main.py:733) and submitted via `runner.run_sync(game_master, conversation, hooks=tool_hooks)` in `_play_turn`, together with the post-refusal cleanup that keeps the conversation and game state unchanged.
contracts.protected_resource: The Game Master agent's input-processing path (its run over the player's message) and the conversation history fed into that run.
contracts.protection_obligation: Player input that constitutes a prompt-injection/manipulation attempt (instruction override, identity reassignment, system-prompt extraction, system-role impersonation, or a novel manipulation per the LLM judge) must never be processed by the Game Master agent: the SDK input guardrail registered on the agent (input_guardrails=[build_injection_guardrail(settings)], backed by deterministic detect_injection patterns plus an LLM injection judge) must trip with GuardrailFunctionOutput(tripwire_triggered=True) before the agent run at runner.run_sync; on InputGuardrailTripwireTriggered the turn must be refused (the model never runs), an in-character refusal notice shown, the blocked message dropped from the conversation history, and the prior scene and game state left unchanged.
scope_limits: Covers only the Game Master input path through `_play_turn`/`runner.run_sync`; meta-commands (stats, inventory, summary, help, new, save/load, debug) never invoke the agent and are outside this contract (src/dungeon_agents/main.py:356-363, 624-729).

The guardrail is registered only on the Game Master; the specialist sub-agents (rules_referee, lore_keeper) run as tools without this input guardrail in the supplied source (src/dungeon_agents/agents/game_master.py:123-144).

Detection coverage is not claimed: layer 1 is a fixed pattern list whose own documentation says it can miss novel phrasings (src/dungeon_agents/domain/guardrails.py:14-18); the contract asserts the trip mechanism and refusal flow, not exhaustive injection detection.

Output-side mechanisms (Character Judge leak review, Critic coherence review, MAX_SCENE_RETRIES regeneration) and tool-level rule enforcement (inventory/gold/HP) are separate obligations and excluded from this contract.

The guarded run, if unblocked, would transitively commit further effects (model API traffic plus tool executions and game-state persistence); the contract's commit point is the run invocation itself, and the downstream strata are not separately guarded commit points in the supplied source.
No runtime behavior or prevalence claims are made; ordering and semantics of the guardrail relative to the model call are asserted by in-repository comments/docstrings only.
